name: Dai Tiantian
current_role: Director, Vice President and Technical Director of Software R&D, Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology (688188.SH)
profile: Dai Tiantian (b. 1983) co-founded Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) in 2007 with four Shanghai Jiao Tong University classmates; it makes the dominant laser-cutting CNC control systems and software (CypCut, TubesT) in China. He chaired the company until 2018 and is now a director, VP and software R&D chief, holding about 14% as one of five joint controllers.
interesting_fact: Friendess began in 2007 as an SJTU student startup with registered capital of just RMB 200,000; it listed on the STAR Market in 2019 among the first batch of companies and became the leading supplier of laser-cutting control systems.
deep_cut_fact: Both his bachelor's (2004) and master's (2007) degrees are from Shanghai Jiao Tong University; at founding he put in RMB 60,000 of the RMB 200,000 capital, six times each co-founder's RMB 10,000, and he holds the Chinese 'senior systems analyst' qualification.
notes: Male (the Hurun name can be misread). Low public profile, technical founder; chairman Tang Ye is the public face. Best route is the company IR mailbox.

name: Sir Evelyn de Rothschild
profile: Former chairman of N M Rothschild & Sons; he died on 7 November 2022. The 2020 Sunday Times listing shared with Lady (Lynn Forester) de Rothschild refers to him.
notes: Died 7 Nov 2022 (Rothschild Archive: https://rothschildarchive.org/archive/staff/sir_evelyn_de_rothschild_1931_2022). The surviving wealth holder is Lady Lynn Forester de Rothschild (E.L. Rothschild / Inclusive Capitalism); research her separately if relevant.

name: Zhong Xiaoxiao
profile: Listed by Hurun (2020-2026) with wealth from Nongfu Spring, the Hangzhou bottled-water company founded and controlled by Zhong Shanshan and listed in Hong Kong in 2020. Repeated searches found no public filing or press item naming Zhong Xiaoxiao or her role, shareholding or relationship to the company.
notes: Identity not verified. She is probably a Nongfu Spring/Yangshengtang shareholder, possibly a relative of Zhong Shanshan, but no source confirms it. She has no public profile. The only institutional route is Nongfu Spring's IR office (HKEX: 9633).

name: Liu Yongliang
current_role: Founder, Executive Director and Chairman, Canggang Railway Ltd (HKEX: 2169)
profile: Liu Yongliang (b. c.1967) founded Canggang Railway, a local freight railway operator in Hebei. Its Canggang line runs from Cangzhou to the Bohai New Area and Huanghua Port and links with the Shuohuang and Hanhuang lines to move mainly coal toward the coast. He has chaired the operating company since 2009 and took the group public in Hong Kong in October 2020. He controls about 40% through Jinghai BVI.
interesting_fact: Before railways, Liu invested in coal trading, industrial property and storage/transport. Canggang now describes itself as Hebei's leading local railway operator and connects the Beijing-Shanghai line to the Bohai New Area.
deep_cut_fact: His education was in military finance: he trained in financial management at the PLA Navy Logistics College in Tianjin (graduated 1991), later did postgraduate finance at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (1999), and attended Peking University's post-EMBA courses from 2012 to 2014.
notes: Hurun lists his country as blank; he is mainland Chinese (Hebei). The only published channel is the company's general contact mailbox (a 126.com address on the official website). He reduced his stake from about 48% to 40% in September 2025.

name: Ke Lei
current_role: Director and Assistant to the President, Keboda Technology Co., Ltd. (603786.SH)
profile: Ke Lei (b. 1985) is a director of Keboda Technology, a Shanghai-based auto-electronics maker (lighting and motor control, energy management, central computing and ADAS domain controllers) that listed in Shanghai in 2019. He is a nephew of the co-controlling founders Ke Guihua and Ke Binghua and acts in concert with them. He owns 25% of Keboda Holding (about 59% of the company) plus about 3% directly.
interesting_fact: Keboda, founded in 2003 by Wenzhou-born entrepreneur Ke Guihua, has moved from lighting control modules into central computing platforms and smart-driving domain controllers.
deep_cut_fact: He started in Keboda's infrastructure/construction department as a supervisor and also ran MRO purchasing. From 2018 he was deputy director of the procurement centre, then worked in the intelligent light-source centre before joining the board.
notes: Low profile, operations-focused next-generation family member. Chairman/president Ke Guihua is the company's public face. Contact through the board office email.

name: Wu Zhongquan
profile: Hurun listed him from 2009 to 2013 as the owner of 'Jindu', a real estate business, most likely Hangzhou-based Jindu Real Estate Group (金都房产集团). He has been off the list since 2013. No current public source could be retrieved to confirm his role or the company's present status.
notes: Not verified. Searches and direct fetches turned up no usable source; the Jindu websites were unreachable or blocked. He dropped off Hurun after 2013, and the private developer may have shrunk. Low priority.

name: Feng Tao
current_role: Founder, Shanghai Yongxuan Venture Capital Management (NewMargin / Lianchuang Yongxuan); co-founding partner, BioTrack Capital (Boyuan) per investor databases
profile: Feng Tao is a veteran Shanghai venture capitalist. He founded NewMargin Ventures (Shanghai Lianchuang) in 1999, one of China's earliest domestic VC firms, which later operated as Lianchuang Yongxuan / Shanghai Yongxuan Venture Capital. By 2015 he said his group managed about RMB 20bn and had taken Beijing Yongxuan public on the New Third Board.
interesting_fact: NewMargin, founded in 1999, was among the first generation of homegrown Chinese VC firms. In 2015 Feng said his group had more than 50 exits via the New Third Board in a single half-year.
deep_cut_fact: At a 2015 industry forum he called the New Third Board China's 'real growth-enterprise board' (真正的创业板), arguing it was built for companies in their growth stage. He cited game developer Wuyou Interactive as a portfolio example.
notes: Common name; the Hurun listing (Yongxuan, investments) matches the Shanghai Yongxuan founder. His later BioTrack Capital role comes only from investor databases and is unconfirmed. No published personal contact; approach through the firm. Off Hurun since 2021.
